blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A great circle is the largest possible circle that can be drawn on a sphere.
The Equator is uniquely the only line of latitude that forms a great circle.
All lines of latitude other than the Equator are classified as small circles.
Great circle routes provide the shortest distance between any two locations on Earth.
Exam questions frequently trap candidates by stating all latitudes are great circles; remember that ONLY the Equator is a great circle.
Great circle routes are specifically tested as the shortest distance between two places, which is why they are standard in aviation and shipping navigation.

blocks.content: Great circle routes provide the shortest distance between two places and are used in aviation and shipping.
